ai_show_review.summary: Blazing blues set with razor‑sharp guitar and crystal‑clear soundboard
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a high‑energy blues‑rock set highlighted by a scorching King Bee > Caution segue, soaring solos on I Know You Rider, and a tight Stealin' finale. Jerry’s razor‑sharp guitar and Phil’s driving bass keep the momentum relentless throughout.
ai_show_review.review: February 25, 1966 at the Ivar Theater captures the Dead in their raw, blues‑driven prime. From the opening “On The Road Again” through a scorching King Bee > Caution transition, the band rides a high tide of energy, with Jerry Garcia’s guitar cutting like a razor and Phil Lesh’s bass anchoring every groove. Pigpen’s organ and harmonica add a gritty texture while Bill Kreutzmann drives the beat with relentless force. Standout moments include soaring leads on “I Know You Rider” and “Hey Little One,” a tight, swinging rendition of “Cold Rain And Snow,” and an inspired second‑half “Stealin’” that feels like a perfect closing statement. Both available recordings are praised for their crystal‑clear fidelity – the soundboard capture especially noted as near CD quality – making this early ’66 performance a must‑listen for anyone tracing the Dead’s evolution from blues roots to psychedelic horizons.
